problems: The carpenter reads primarily as a belted modern shirt over straight trousers; the fallen hood contributes almost nothing to the visible silhouette.
The breadmaker's two narrow apron straps resemble suspenders, while the solid pale cylinder reads as a disc rather than a bowl or bread.
The elder's disconnected front mantle panels resemble an oversized bow tie rather than a continuous medieval shoulder garment.
The messenger's hood reads as a pointed cap: its neck coverage and trailing hood shape are insufficiently visible.
The breadmaker and elder have long, single hip-bound boxes enclosing both legs. Walking clearance is unproven, with a substantial risk of legs breaking through the rigid garments.

The jester reads immediately as a performer, but the small chest diamond does little to distinguish a visiting court from a local entertainer. Important costume contrasts also depend on unspecified avatar colours.

Medieval is only clear on 2 of the 6 kits. The Breadmaker (long dress, apron, coif) and the Jester (motley, three-point cap) read as medieval. The Carpenter and the Messenger look like a red or green T-shirt with a belt over blue jeans: the 'pants' role renders denim-blue under a mid-thigh shirt, so the silhouette says modern.

Carpenter: the 'fallen hood' (a cape-bone box 0.36x0.23x0.18 tucked behind the shoulders) can't be seen. Only a yellow sliver shows beside the head, so the bible's 'hood pushed back' is missing. The slanted 'hair' slab on the head reads as a flat-top or a scowling brow bar.

Carpenter: the mallet hangs head-down below the hand as a dark #5c4030 box (0.26x0.14x0.14) with the handle sticking up through the hand. At stream scale it reads as a lunchbox or handbag, not a tool.

Carpenter and Messenger are nearly the same kit: same thigh-length tunic, same brown belt, same 'pants' legs, same shirt colours. Only the headgear and a small satchel differ, which fails 'four kits clearly different'. From above, the Carpenter is a plain coloured rectangle.

Breadmaker: the loaf is a flat grey (#c5c0a8) disc 0.31 wide, sticking out sideways from the left hand. It reads as a plate, a stone or a frisbee, not bread. The dark 'hair' bar across the forehead under the coif looks like an angry unibrow.
Market Elder: the hat (a cylinder plus a tilted box in the 'hat' colour) renders as a lumpy yellow or ochre blob, close to a pile of cheese or a modern beret. It has no medieval hat shape.

Market Elder: the beard is a black box sitting mostly below the head (y -0.005 on the head bone), so it reads as a gaping black mouth. It is the wearer's hair colour, so it is never grey, which undercuts 'elder'. The two separate shoulder boxes look like modern lapels or shoulder pads, not a mantle. On the second wearer the accent renders a saturated royal/violet blue that falls outside the muted palette.
Market Elder: the staff knob sits at shoulder height next to the face. Seen from above at 40 degrees the staff hardly rises past the head, so the strongest silhouette cue is wasted.

Young Messenger: the 'pointed hood' liripipe (a cone rotated -0.95 on x) renders as a vertical spike on a boxy cap. With a yellow 'hat' colour it reads as a gold spiked helmet or Pickelhaube, the knight/soldier read the bible avoids. The hood's capelet (a cape-bone box) is hidden behind the back.
Young Messenger: the scroll is a cylinder rotated 90 degrees on z, so it pokes straight out sideways from the left hand behind the satchel. It reads as a cigarette or stray white stick.

King: the tunic uses 'shirt' and the cloak uses 'accent'. On the rendered wearer both are red, so the tunic and cloak merge into one red mass. The bible asks for a deep blue tunic and a red cloak. The tunic is the same thigh length as the Carpenter's, which is not grand.

King: the crown cylinder is 0.46 wide against a 0.30 head, with 6 cones in a front and a back row. From the front it reads as a spiky golden afro or hedgehog, from above as a gold disc. The ermine collar is two separate pale boxes that look like pillows or shoulder pads. The fur edges of the cloak show only as pale strips behind the arms, like loose white sleeves.

King: the sceptre (a cylinder from y +0.06 to -0.52 on armR) runs up along the arm with the orb floating beside the shoulder. It looks fused to the sleeve rather than held. The Jester's baton has the same fault.

Jester: the cap's base band uses the 'hat' role, which renders gold. With the stiff upright centre cone it reads as a gold crown, so the leader's head silhouette competes with the King's. The marotte (a brown cone on a brown sphere) reads as a torch or club. The travel patch uses 'shirt:light', which renders pink, like a bandage or skin. The curled toes (rotation -0.65, tucked into the shoe) can't be seen. Apart from the badge, nothing says 'travelled from far away'.
fix:
Carpenter: Make the tunic visibly longer than a shirt, with a stepped or split hem over close-fitting hose. Enlarge the fallen hood into a connected neck-and-shoulder roll with a visible folded tail down the back. Keep the belt and wooden mallet. Breadmaker: Replace the vertical straps with a clear waist-apron tie over the long gown. Fit the linen coif closely around the sides and back of the head. Replace the pale disc with a chunky scored loaf or a shallow bowl with a contrasting recessed interior. Use an articulated skirt or overlapping lower panels that accommodate each leg. Market Elder: Join the front panels across the shoulders to the back mantle, forming one broad, sloping garment rather than two bow-tie tabs; retain one central clasp. Keep the cap and staff, and articulate the long robe for walking. Messenger: Extend the hood around the cheeks and onto the shoulders; lower and tilt its point backwards into a trailing liripipe. Preserve the short tunic, tall boots and satchel, ensuring the strap visibly meets the bag. King: Preserve the crown, sceptre and broad contrasting cloak. Join the cream shoulder pieces into a continuous fur yoke and verify cloak clearance during arm swings and walking. Far-Court Jester: Preserve the three-point bell cap and divided costume. Guarantee strong light–dark separation between its colour halves, enlarge the diamond into a bold visiting-court device, and repeat it on a short shoulder tab visible from above. Check all six outfits on both body variants in walking poses and at actual stream scale. / GLOBAL: never leave bare 'pants' legs under a short tunic. Give every everyday kit hose on legL and legR (box [0,-0.36,0] size [0.19,0.62,0.21]) in a fixed palette colour per kit, not the 'pants' role, so nobody reads as wearing jeans. Delete the forehead 'hair' bars (Carpenter, Breadmaker). Keep hats and hoods in 'hat:dark' or fixed palette cloth so they never render gold, because gold belongs only to the King's crown.

CARPENTER: (1) Lengthen and flare the tunic skirt: hips box [0,-0.17,0] size [0.54,0.36,0.33]. (2) Make the fallen hood read as a cowl around the neck: hips box [0,0.6,-0.03] size [0.52,0.12,0.36] in 'hat:dark'. Hang a hood bag on the cape bone: box [0,-0.12,0] size [0.34,0.28,0.12]. Add a liripipe tail: cape box [0,-0.4,0] size [0.07,0.3,0.05]. (3) Hose in fixed #8b6240, with turnshoes and ankle wraps: legL and legR box [0,-0.72,0.04] size [0.21,0.16,0.28] in #5c4030. (4) Add a leather half-apron: hips box [0,-0.12,0.17] size [0.36,0.42,0.03] in #8b6240. (5) Replace the hanging mallet with a timber plank on the right shoulder, on the hips bone so it doesn't swing: box [-0.2,0.64,0] size [0.12,0.08,1.0] in #c5c0a8 or a light wood colour. Or keep a mallet with the head ABOVE the hand: handle cylinder [0,-0.5,0.14] size [0.05,0.4,0.05], rotation [-0.6,0,0], with a light-wood head box at its upper end.

BREADMAKER: (1) Replace the grey disc with a domed loaf cradled in front: armL sphere [0,-0.46,0.14] size [0.26,0.16,0.22] in #8b6240, with a #d6af55 top-cap sphere slightly smaller. Better still, a flat tray of three loaves held at the waist, or carried on the head over the coif (head box [0,0.42,0] size [0.42,0.04,0.36] in #8b6240 plus three small #d6af55 spheres), which reads strongly from above. (2) Long sleeves: armL and armR box [0,-0.2,0] size [0.15,0.42,0.17] in 'shirt'. (3) Flare the hem with a second box [0,-0.62,0] size [0.62,0.16,0.4] so her silhouette differs from the Elder's straight robe. Keep the coif and apron; they work.

MARKET ELDER: (1) Replace the lumpy hat with a hood-and-shoulder-cape (chaperon): head box covering the top and sides [0,0.24,-0.02] size [0.36,0.18,0.34], plus hips box [0,0.52,0] size [0.6,0.16,0.4], both in 'accent:dark'. Or use a tall felt hat: a brim cylinder [0,0.33,0] size [0.42,0.04,0.40] and a crown cylinder [0,0.43,0] size [0.28,0.2,0.26]. (2) Beard in #c5c0a8 (grey), attached to the face: head box [0,0.0,0.15] size [0.22,0.22,0.05], top edge at the mouth line, plus a tapered tip box below it. (3) Replace the two shoulder boxes with one continuous mantle wrap: hips box [0,0.5,0.0] size [0.6,0.14,0.38] plus a front drape [0,0.38,0.17] size [0.42,0.12,0.04], in fixed #405e8b or #416c48 instead of the saturated accent. (4) Raise the staff so the knob sits above head height (top at about +0.45 on the arm bone; size y 1.6). Add a crook or forked top so it reads from above.

YOUNG MESSENGER: (1) Rebuild the hood so it's soft: head shell box [0,0.25,-0.02] size [0.36,0.16,0.34] plus side panels. Drop the vertical cone. Make the liripipe a tail hanging down the back: a cape-bone box [0,-0.15,0.02] size [0.07,0.45,0.05], or a cone on the head at [0,0.18,-0.22] with rotation [2.4,0,0] so it points down and back. Add a short hood capelet with a jagged (dagged) edge on the hips bone [0,0.52,0] size [0.58,0.14,0.38] plus 4-5 small boxes rotated 0.785 along its hem. Colour 'hat:dark' or fixed #416c48, never a role that can go gold. (2) Hose in a fixed colour contrasting with the Carpenter's (#416c48 or #9e443e), with tall turned-down boots (cuff box at the top). (3) Scroll held upright: armL cylinder [0,-0.48,0.1] size [0.07,0.26,0.07], no z rotation, in #e5d8b6, with a #9e443e seal sphere. (4) Replace the belt and buckle with a crossbody strap only, and give the satchel a lighter flap, so it no longer matches the Carpenter.

KING: (1) Use fixed colours. Long robe to the ankles in #405e8b (hips box [0,-0.36,0] size [0.56,0.82,0.36]); cloak in #9e443e. The head is one person, so consistency beats personal colour. (2) Crown band sized to the head: cylinder [0,0.37,0] size [0.36,0.1,0.34] in #d6af55. Put 5 taller points ONLY around the rim (cones 0.08 wide, 0.16 high, radius 0.17, front and sides). Add a red velvet cap inside: cylinder [0,0.41,0] size [0.28,0.12,0.26] in #9e443e, so it reads as a crown from above. Add a single red front jewel. (3) One continuous ermine collar wrapping the shoulders: hips box [0,0.57,-0.02] size [0.66,0.12,0.4] in #e5d8b6, with 4-6 tiny #343b40 ermine spots. Widen the cloak to 0.72 and bring its front edges forward to z 0.05 so the red shows beside the arms from the front. (4) Sceptre angled out of the hand: armR cylinder [0,-0.5,0.2] size [0.05,0.5,0.05], rotation [-1.0,0,0], with a gold orb or fleur at the far end, clearly forward of the body and above the hand.

JESTER: (1) Cap band in cloth, not 'hat': two halves in 'shirt' and 'accent', extended down the sides as a hood (head boxes at x ±0.17, y 0.18, size [0.06,0.26,0.3]). (2) All three points floppy: side cones rotated about ±1.3 so they droop outward and down, back cone rotated [-1.2,0,0] to droop backward, bells at the tips. No upright centre spike. (3) Marotte angled forward: armL cylinder [0,-0.5,0.2], rotation [-0.9,0,0], in #8b6240. Top it with a skin-tone sphere (the fool's head) wearing two tiny shirt/accent cones. (4) Patch in #8b6240 or #e5d8b6, plus a second patch on the opposite sleeve. (5) Visible curled toes: legL and legR box [0,-0.7,0.26] size [0.1,0.08,0.16], rotation [-1.0,0,0], each with a small #d6af55 bell sphere. (6) Add a dagged collar: 6 small boxes rotated 0.785 around the neck in alternating shirt/accent. Add a travel bundle on the back: cape box [0,-0.25,-0.1] size [0.32,0.34,0.2] in #8b6240 with a #e5d8b6 bedroll cylinder across the top. Together these say 'from far away' from above.
